A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNA unlearning study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original RNA experiments on WMDP and MMLU, including robustness, alignment, noise-injection and cross-model evaluations.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds regularization comparisons, knowledge-recovery experiments, chain-of-thought evaluations and MUSE-News results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 still adds Gaussian noise to reference-model retain representations and uses the resulting representations or logits as retain-loss targets. The RNA procedure and its RM/PO components remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v5 adds GSM8K and GPQA reasoning evaluations with chain-of-thought prompting, MUSE-News open-ended unlearning, and knowledge-recovery scenarios. WMDP/MMLU, the eight alignment benchmarks and multi-token perturbations were already evaluated in v4.

E2.justification: New Table 2 evaluates weight decay and dropout as alternatives to RNA across all nine unlearning methods, substantially expanding the controls beyond v4's original-versus-RNA comparisons. The original RM/PO comparator families remain.

E3.justification: v5 introduces LoRA recovery experiments using 5–1000 examples, zero/four/eight-shot CoT evaluations, and MUSE open-ended protocols with KnowMem and VerbMem metrics. Existing unlearning settings also change their reported optimizer from AdamW to Adam in Appendix A.4 and the additional-model section; the PDFs do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds relearning, benign-finetuning and four white-box recovery tests, CoT side-effect analyses, and over-/under-unlearning experiments. Appendix C.2 replaces generated-token maximum-activation histograms with PCA analysis of query-token latent perturbations. Earlier n-gram and injection-layer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Colored table annotations remain score differences rather than uncertainty estimates; the distribution plots are mechanism diagnostics.

E6.justification: v5 adds regularization, recovery, CoT and MUSE results while retaining the numerical content of the matched older tables and plots. For example, new Table 13 reports that RNA at RMU c=150 and noise scale 0.001 raises benign-retain KnowMem from 18.0 to 43.5 while also raising forget KnowMem from 13.7 to 48.6. This is an added experiment, not a same-setting version-to-version gain.

T1.justification: Equation 10 replaces v4's generic objective using original representation targets with explicitly weighted poisoned-forget and benign-retain losses incorporating transformed forget targets. The Taylor analysis, Gaussian assumptions and both robustness theorems and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: unlearning-induced fragility, the unified RM/PO and backdoor perspectives, and RNA improving retain-robustness while preserving forget/retain performance. Reorganized contributions and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v5 explains how latent smoothing may facilitate relearning and identifies poorly calibrated unlearning as a failure condition, including recovery of both forget and retain knowledge. Section 5 also clarifies that the backdoor analogy concerns inadvertent representation alignment rather than acquisition of new malicious capabilities.

D1.justification: v5 adds LoRA relearning configurations, recovery-attack construction and hyperparameters, regularizer settings, and MUSE checkpoint, prompting and training details. The code link is retained in a different location, while v4's promised future release of perturbed MMLU data is omitted; this does not establish an actual withdrawal.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for regularization, recovery methods, reasoning benchmarks and recent unlearning research. It newly relates RNA's latent-space smoothing to parameter-space SAM and Damian et al.'s smoothing analysis. The central positioning around retain-robustness remains unchanged; publication updates are not new works.

P1.justification: v5 edits the abstract, threat-model explanations, headings and author information, separates RNA into Section 6, and moves alignment and broader-impact discussions into the main text. Much of the existing exposition remains intact despite these organizational refinements.

P2.justification: The journal format changes typography, headers and page composition. v5 adds recovery plots, an open-ended prompt illustration and several experimental tables, replaces the maximum-activation figure with PCA panels, and moves the alignment table into the main text. Most earlier plot graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 addresses important gaps in v4 through regularization controls, knowledge-recovery attacks and MUSE miscalibration experiments. Evidence that RNA can accelerate relearning or restore forgotten knowledge substantially clarifies its limitations, while CoT evaluations and more direct latent diagnostics strengthen empirical coverage. These gains outweigh remaining documentation problems, including the unexplained optimizer revision and reversed loss-weight descriptions in Appendix J.
